About me

Science across disciplines

I am an astrophysicist with a PhD from Heidelberg University (2022). My doctoral research focused on discovering and characterizing exoplanets orbiting M-dwarf stars, combining photometric data from NASA’s TESS mission with high-precision radial velocities from CARMENES.

Since 2022, I have worked at Freie Universität Berlin as part of the PLATO Mission Consortium Calibration Operations Team (PCOT) for ESA’s PLATO mission. I contribute to scientific and technical preparations for mission operations, connecting astronomical research with instrument calibration, operational planning and verification.

I also enjoy teaching, communicating science and collaborating across disciplines to make astronomy accessible to broader audiences.

Research & Projects

From discovering planets to preparing missions

My career bridges observational astrophysics, instrumentation, data analysis and space mission operations.

ESA · PLATO

Payload Calibration & Operations

As a member of PCOT since 2022, I contribute to calibration reference target selection, commissioning strategies, instrument health monitoring through Quick Look Analysis (QLA), operational tool verification, and coordination with mission science and engineering teams.

Exoplanet science

Discovering and characterizing distant worlds

My doctoral work combined TESS transit photometry and CARMENES radial-velocity observations to study small planets around cool stars. My first-author research includes the exoplanet systems TOI-1235 and TOI-1685.

Observational exoplanet science

Scientific Data & Observational Methods

My research focuses on combining complementary observational techniques to detect and characterize exoplanets, particularly small planets orbiting M-dwarf stars.

Transit photometry

When a planet passes in front of its host star, it blocks a small fraction of the starlight, producing a measurable dip in brightness. The depth and timing of these dips constrain the planet’s radius, orbital period and geometry. Repeated observations can reveal additional planets and variations in their transit times.

In my doctoral research, I worked with NASA TESS photometry, including light-curve extraction and correction from target-pixel files and full-frame images, detrending and transit modelling.

High-resolution spectroscopy & radial velocities

A planet’s gravitational pull causes its star to move around their common centre of mass. High-resolution spectra reveal this motion through tiny Doppler shifts in stellar absorption lines. The radial-velocity signal constrains the planet’s minimum mass; for a transiting planet, the orbital inclination helps determine its true mass. Combined with its radius, this provides an estimate of bulk density.

I analysed radial-velocity time series from CARMENES and worked with spectroscopic data reduction and radial-velocity extraction using instruments including FEROS and PUCHEROS. My analysis involved Python-based workflows and modelling of stellar and planetary signals.

Illustrations supplied for this website; the transit example is an illustrative planetary-system animation, not an observation of TOI-1235 or TOI-1685.

PLATO mission operations

Mission Tools, Calibration & Instrumentation

Within the PLATO Mission Consortium Calibration Operations Team (PCOT), I contribute to calibration and science operations through five interconnected areas. Select a card to explore my work.

Quick Look Analysis

Defining QLA monitoring parameters, visualisations and alert criteria to track instrument performance and identify potential anomalies.

Calibration Reference Targets

Defined requirements and selection criteria for PLATO calibration reference targets, contributed to the calibration input catalogues paper (Heller et al. 2026), and used Python to analyse the distribution of reference samples on the PLATO camera detectors.

Commissioning

Supporting commissioning and fine-tuning strategies, connecting scientific requirements to instrument calibration.

Operational Tools

Testing the Manual Commanding Tool (MCT), commanding workflows and the generation of Consortium Operational Requests (CORs).

Interface Coordination

Coordinating with the ESA Science Operations Centre and combining scientific requirements, Python-based analysis and operational verification.

International collaboration

Science–engineering interfaces

Working across scientific institutions and technical teams, translating research needs into operational requirements and contributing to shared mission documentation and testing campaigns.

Teaching & Outreach

Sharing the universe

University teaching

Teaching and mentoring experience at Freie Universität Berlin, Heidelberg University, the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy, and universities in Chile. Topics include exoplanets, observational astronomy, astrophysics and physics.

Public engagement

Experience in astronomy outreach for audiences of different ages, including an inclusive astronomy initiative for children with visual impairments and hands-on educational activities in Chile.

Science, culture & art

I am interested in interdisciplinary approaches that connect astronomical discoveries with creative expression, visual interpretation and public understanding of science.

Scientific computing & data analysis

Python-based scientific computing for astronomical data analysis, including light-curve extraction and detrending, transit and radial-velocity modelling, spectroscopic data reduction, and reproducible workflows for interpreting observational data.

Observational experience

Hands-on telescope experience at ground-based observatories, including La Silla (FEROS), Las Campanas (du Pont Telescope), the Very Large Telescope (VLT; NACO), and Observatorio UC at Santa Martina (PUCHEROS).
